checks: For the six listed direction vectors, all consecutive and one-skipped oriented determinants are 1. Thus D_i=R_iR_{i+1} and E_i=R_{i−1}R_{i+1}, and subtracting the adjacent h_i terms leaves the diagonal c_{i−1}+c_i−R_i⁻². All six gaps are less than π.

The horizontal intercepts are A=Br/(B+r) and −a=−bt/(b+t), both lying inside their respective chord segments. The four fixed core areas give zero consecutive matrix couplings on sectors 0, 2, 3 and 5. The diagonals at nodes 0 and 3 are zero by the same intercept identities.

The remaining diagonals are u+α, u+β, v+β and v+α, and are strictly positive for finite allowed X,Y. Their off-diagonals are u−1/(Bt) and v−1/(br). The two-by-two determinants therefore decide PSD. At a core lower equality the corresponding off-diagonal is zero and the two scalar blocks are positive.

Writing d=Bt and e=br, αβ=1/(de), while α+β+2/d=(bt+Br+2e)/(de) and α+β+2/e=(bt+Br+2d)/(de). The determinant numerators yield exactly X≤d(bt+Br+2e)/(2(e−d)) for e>d and Y≤e(bt+Br+2d)/(2(d−e)) for d>e. The other determinant is positive, and for d=e both determinants are positive for all finite allowed areas. Each restrictive bound is strictly above its core lower bound.

With both lower bounds strict, only sectors 1 and 4 contribute insertion vertices. The least eigenvector choice puts the same slack, the least eigenvalue, at every node in its block. Thus the two singleton nodes remain straight, and the ray vertices number four in the strict region or two when exactly one finite bound is attained. This count is for the specified construction.

The cap sector lists are (0,4,5), (0,1,2) and (2,3,4). The vertical and horizontal chord lengths give B+b and A+a. The diagonal chord has length √2(r+t) and normal norm √2, so its coarea length is r+t.
